title: A live-imaging protocol for tracking intestinal stem cell divisions in the Drosophila melanogaster pupal midgut
protocol: Heat the metal bath to 37°C.
Melt the LIG on the heated metal bath for 10 minutes.
Cut a 22 mm × 22 mm coverslip into two equal pieces from the middle.
Pipette 10 μL of melted LIG onto the dish.
Quickly cover the LIG with one pre-cut coverslip.
Repeat steps to pipette and cover the other side of the dish, spacing the coverslips approximately 5 mm apart.
Gently pry several properly staged pupae from the side of the vial using a brush.
Transfer these pupae to the dissecting plate.
Place the pupae under a dissecting microscope.
Add 40 μL of LIB to the center of a dissecting plate.
Transfer one pupa into the LIB under a dissecting microscope.
Gently grasp the anterior part of the pupa with a dull flat-ended forceps.
Press down very gently on the top of the meconium with another pair of fine-tipped forceps, keeping them open.
Divide the pupa into two parts from the insertion position carefully.
Remove the head of the pupa by holding the head and neck with two pairs of forceps and pulling in opposite directions.
Peel off the anterior shell.
Peel off the posterior shell.
Gently rinse the midgut by aspirating LIB through a 200 μL pipette.
Grasp the pupa from the anterior part using one pair of blunt, flat-ended forceps.
Insert one tip of fine-tipped forceps onto the top of the meconium.
Pull back to expose the midgut without breaking it.
Remove the head of the pupa by holding the head and neck with two pairs of forceps respectively and pulling in opposite directions.
Use flat-ended forceps to gently press down on the surface of the pupa to hold it in place.
Use fine-tipped forceps to peel off the anterior shell.
Wash the 20 μL strippette tip 3 times with LIB.
Gently aspirate the dissected pupal midgut (in LIB) under the microscope using a 20 μL pipette gun.
Transfer the dissected pupal midgut together with associated tissues in LIB to the gap between the two coverslips using the pipette gun.
Add 10 μL of 37°C LIG to the transferred midgut.
Gently mix with LIB and aspirate 10 μL of the mixed liquid.
Discard the mixed liquid.
Adjust the position of the midgut so that it is not folded.
Repeat steps adding, mixing, discarding, and adjusting twice more.
Add 20 μL of 37°C LIG to the space between two 11 × 22 mm coverslips.
Quickly cover the midgut with a 22 × 22 mm coverslip using forceps.
Press the 22 × 22 mm coverslip gently to stabilize it close to the midgut.
Allow LIG to solidify for 2 minutes at 25°C.
Seal the 22 × 22 mm coverslips with approximately 80 μL of halocarbon oil 27 using a 20 μL pipette gun.
Place the live imaging dish without a lid, with the coverslip upside down so that the objective touches the coverslip.
Image the mounted live imaging dish on a Zeiss LSM 800 confocal microscope using a Plan-Apochromat 63x/1.40 Oil DIC M27 objective and Immersol 518 F imaging medium.
Use definite focus to avoid focus drift.
Acquire time-lapse images using ZEN 2.1 with the time-lapse module.
Take an image of the pupal midgut from the parts indicated by rectangles.
Set laser wavelengths for green and red channels at 488 nm and 561 nm, respectively.
Adjust laser power to 2% for the green channel and 0.2% for the red channel.
Set detection wavelengths to 410-525 nm for the green channel and 580–700 nm for the red channel.
Acquire 8–12 μm z-stack images (2 μm intervals) of 512 × 512 pixels (0.198 μm × 0.198 μm).
Acquire images every 60 seconds with a pixel time of 1.03 μs.
Adjust the total imaging time according to experimental requirements and imaging needs.
Image the midgut in Drosophila pupae at 25°C.
Place the mounted dish in 50°C hot water for 5 minutes after imaging.
Rinse the dish with water and dry it before reuse.
